newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean union leader warns of new strike.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean union leader warns of new strike.

text.p: The leader of South Korea's outlawed union group, addressing tens of thousands of workers in Seoul on Sunday, pledged to bring forward a planned strike unless the government scrapped a controversial new labour law.

"If our demands are not met we warn we will launch an all-out stoppage originally planned for February 18 earlier than that," Kwon Young-kil told more than 50,000 workers and their families in the largest protest rally since the bill was rammed through parliament on December 26.
Police estimated 55,000 protesters were gathered on a vast strip of concrete running past the capital's financial centre.
The Korean Confederation of Trade Unions and the officially-sanctioned Federation of Korean Trade Unions, which jointly organised the demonstration, put the figure at 200,000.
President Kim Young-sam, bowing to pressure from more than four weeks of strikes, last week agreed to send the labour bill back to parliament for revision. But he insisted it would not be voided.
The confederation is maintaining its pressure on the government with one day of strikes each week on Wednesdays.
